questions.stem: Which version of ISO-8583 does the page say added support for chip cards?

options.says: Not this one. The page calls 1987 the first version, the one that laid the foundation; chip cards appear only under 2003.
Not this one. The page says 1993 brought new data elements and clarifications, and it names chip cards only under 2003.
Right. Section 1.2.3 lists support for new transaction types and technologies among what 2003 added, and chip cards are its example.

questions.stem: The page says the 1993 version introduced new data elements and refined existing ones. What does it say those changes were meant to better support?

options.text: Evolving transaction types and security requirements
options.says: Right. Section 1.2.2 says the 1993 version's new and refined data elements were there to better support evolving transaction types and security requirements.

options.text: Chip cards and other new technologies
options.says: Not this one. The page names chip cards as an example of what the 2003 version added, not as the aim of the 1993 changes.
Not this one. The page lists flexibility for regional variations and future innovations among the 2003 version's improvements.

options.text: Faster adoption of new payment technologies across regions
options.says: Not this one. The page gives that as a reason the standard matters for global standardization, not as the aim of the 1993 version.

questions.stem: The page credits ISO-8583 with faster adoption of new payment technologies across different regions. Which of the standard's benefits does it list that under?

options.text: Global standardization, as a common language for financial institutions worldwide
options.says: Right. Section 1.3.1 lists faster adoption of new payment technologies across regions as one reason the standard matters for global standardization.
Not this one. The page's interoperability list is about communication between banks, cross-border use, new players and value-added services, not the adoption of new technologies.

options.text: Its role in electronic financial transactions
options.says: Not this one. The page's list of roles covers a standardized format, structured data, real-time authorization, clearing and settlement, and the range of transaction types.
